title: Pandemic Impacts Through Social Systems
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
A global health emergency does not affect society through biology alone. The virus that causes COVID-19 created a health hazard, but actual outcomes also depended on exposure, age and health, access to care, public information, individual behavior, workplace organization, and government response. The World Health Organization characterized the outbreak as a pandemic on 11 March 2020. That classification described the global spread and seriousness of the situation; it did not prescribe one identical policy for every country.

Economic effects followed several pathways. Illness removed people from work. Distancing rules and voluntary caution reduced activity in contact-intensive services. Supply interruptions limited production elsewhere, while demand shifted toward some goods and digital services. Governments and central banks then chose support measures with different designs and timing. It is therefore imprecise to label every economic change “the effect of the virus.” Some changes were direct, some were mediated by responses, and some reflected vulnerabilities that existed before the emergency.

The same distinction matters in education and employment. Remote systems preserved some continuity, yet access to devices, quiet space, broadband, adaptable teaching, and secure employment was unequal. A person able to work from home faced a different risk set from a worker whose income required physical presence. An average measure of school closure or working hours can reveal scale, but it can hide who lost instruction, income, care time, or health protection.

Good evaluation must also respect measurement limits. Reported cases depend on testing and reporting; reported deaths and excess mortality answer related but different questions. A change observed after 2020 may also reflect demographic trends, energy prices, later conflicts, or earlier inequalities. The deeper lesson is institutional: resilience is not merely returning to the previous average. It is the capacity to maintain essential functions, protect people with fewer resources, learn from error, and adapt without making temporary emergency powers permanent by default.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Biology alone determined every social outcome.

options.label: B
options.text: All countries were instructed to use one identical policy.

options.label: C
options.text: Pandemic impacts arose through multiple health, behavioral, policy, and institutional pathways with unequal effects.

options.label: D
options.text: Average statistics reveal every distributional loss.

questions.answer: 正解：C。健康、行動、政策、制度を通る複数経路と不均等な影響が主題です。Aは多経路、Bは分類と処方の区別、Dは平均値の限界を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why should WHO's characterization of a pandemic be distinguished from a policy prescription?

options.label: A
options.text: The classification described global spread and seriousness, while specific policies required national legal, epidemiological, medical, and cost-benefit judgments.

options.label: B
options.text: The classification legally required every country to adopt one identical measure.

options.label: C
options.text: A pandemic classification says nothing about global spread.

options.label: D
options.text: National health-system capacity is irrelevant to policy choice.

questions.answer: 正解：A。国際的分類は状況の性質を記述し、具体策は各国の流行、法制度、医療能力、費用便益に依存します。B～Dは記述と政策判断を混同します。

questions.prompt: The phrase “mediated by responses” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: occurring through actions taken in response

options.label: B
options.text: measured without any assumptions

options.label: C
options.text: caused only by biological infection

options.label: D
options.text: unrelated to institutions

questions.answer: 正解：A。感染から結果へ直接進むだけでなく、距離行動、慎重な消費、政策などの反応を介して生じるという意味です。B～Dは媒介経路を否定します。

questions.prompt: Which set contains three distinct economic pathways identified in the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Illness reducing labor, caution reducing contact services, and supply interruptions limiting production

options.label: B
options.text: Only biological infection, repeated three times

options.label: C
options.text: Identical demand for every good, uninterrupted supply, and no policy response

options.label: D
options.text: School grades, treaty negotiation, and territorial partition

questions.answer: 正解：A。労働供給減、対面サービス縮小、供給網中断は別経路です。ほかにも需要移動や支援策があります。BとCは経路差を消し、Dは本文の経済経路ではありません。

questions.prompt: How does including pre-existing institutional vulnerability improve causal explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: It explains why the same hazard produced different outcomes and helps separate newly created inequality from amplified prior inequality.

options.label: B
options.text: It proves that the emergency itself had no effects.

options.label: C
options.text: It makes health care, job security, housing, and broadband irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees that every country had the same exposure and protection.

questions.answer: 正解：A。医療、雇用保障、通信、住環境の既存差を含めると、同じ危険源でも結果が違う理由と格差の増幅過程を説明できます。B～Dは多因果性を否定します。

questions.prompt: Why can averages of school closure or working hours fail to reveal inequality?

options.label: A
options.text: The same duration can conceal different access to remote learning, income protection, care burdens, and health risks.

options.label: B
options.text: An average always identifies exactly who suffered each type of loss.

options.label: C
options.text: Devices, broadband, quiet space, and job security were distributed equally.

options.label: D
options.text: Distributional information is unnecessary once scale is known.

questions.answer: 正解：A。同じ休校日数・労働時間でも遠隔環境、所得保障、ケア負担、健康リスクが異なり、平均は損失の主体と種類を隠します。B～Dは分布差を否定します。

questions.prompt: Why should reported deaths and excess mortality not be treated as identical measures?

options.label: A
options.text: Reported deaths depend on diagnosis and classification, while excess mortality compares deaths with a modeled baseline and may include indirect effects.

options.label: B
options.text: They use exactly the same data, assumptions, and question in every setting.

options.label: C
options.text: Excess mortality contains no model assumptions.

options.label: D
options.text: Reported deaths are independent of testing and reporting systems.

questions.answer: 正解：A。報告死亡は診断・分類制度、超過死亡は平常時予測モデルとの差に依存し、間接影響も含み得ます。B～Dは問いと誤差構造の差を消します。

questions.prompt: What does the passage mean by saying resilience is not merely returning to the previous average?

options.label: A
options.text: Resilience includes maintaining essential functions, protecting people with fewer resources, learning, adapting, and limiting temporary powers.

options.label: B
options.text: Resilience means restoring aggregate output while ignoring distribution and institutions.

options.label: C
options.text: Resilience requires making every emergency power permanent.

options.label: D
options.text: Resilience excludes learning from error.

questions.answer: 正解：A。必須機能の維持、弱い立場の保護、誤りからの学習、適応、緊急権限の抑制を含む制度能力です。B～Dは本文が退ける狭い回復観です。

questions.prompt: Which preparedness score best follows the passage's argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A score covering surveillance, care capacity, worker protection, paid leave, school continuity, broadband, equitable support, learning mechanisms, and sunset rules

options.label: B
options.text: A score based only on national average output after the crisis

options.label: C
options.text: A score that ignores occupation, income, age, disability, and region

options.label: D
options.text: A score rewarding permanent emergency powers and unreported errors

questions.answer: 正解：A。医療・生活継続・分配・学習・権限統制を危機前後で測る包括的指標です。Bは平均だけ、Cは格差、Dは透明性と一時性を無視します。
